Telluride House at Cornell University, Ithaca NY -- the Telluride Association's flagship, namesake, NRHP-listed building (built 1910). Cornell is confirmed as one of TASS's 2026 host campuses (the other being University of Maryland, per a web search of tellurideassociation.org's own TASS page). TASS rotates among host campuses each year, so this depicts one current host, not a fixed single site -- consistent with this record's own host_institution field ('Rotates among US university host campuses').

UWC Mostar campus entrance (Gimnazija Mostar building), Bosnia and Herzegovina -- a generic UWC-network campus/community photo, NOT specific to Short Courses (which run at varying UWC colleges/national committees worldwide per this record's own host_institution field; confirmed no Short-Courses-specific photo exists on Commons via direct search, zero relevant results). Historic building facade with a sign reading 'GIMNAZIJA MOSTAR' and, below it, a smaller sign with a circular UWC logo plus 'UNITED WORLD COLLEGE' and 'MOSTAR' -- entity confirmed by directly reading this signage. CROSS-LANE NOTE: per this dry run's brief, S7 may have already sourced a separate generic UWC photo elsewhere in its own corpus; I independently checked S7's own photo-sourcing files in this worktree (s7photo_g1/g2/g3_batch1.jsonl, s7_photo_MASTER.jsonl) and found no UWC entry there as of this session (2026-08-27), so could not cross-check or reuse it directly -- this is an independently-sourced candidate. Either image is likely fine to use interchangeably as a generic UWC-network illustration if S7's turns up later.

Pembroke College, Oxford -- entrance screen/gates on Pembroke Square. Pembroke College (together with Corpus Christi College) is the confirmed host college for 'The Oxford Tradition,' one of Oxbridge Academic Programs' five city-based programs (Oxford, Cambridge, Paris, Barcelona, New York). This record's own host_institution field already flags the multi-site structure and that the program is 'not affiliated with the University of Oxford... as an institution' -- that remains accurate: Oxbridge Academic Programs uses the college as a venue/lessee, it is not part of the University of Oxford. Oxford was also the program's founding location ('What began in 1986 as a summer program in Oxford' per oxbridgeprograms.com), making it a reasonable representative choice among the 5 sites rather than an arbitrary pick.

Towers Hall, Otterbein University (Westerville, OH) -- one of the Ross Mathematics Program's two confirmed concurrent 2026 host sites (the other being Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, Terre Haute IN), matching this record's own host_institution field verbatim ('2026: Otterbein University, Columbus, OH AND Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, Terre Haute, IN'). NRHP-listed Gothic Revival building, built 1872. ALTERNATE candidate also independently verified: File:The Ross Mathematics Program in 2012.jpg -- sourced directly from rossprogram.org itself, an official group photo with '2012 Ross Mathematics Program' captioned directly into the image (about the strongest possible in-frame entity confirmation short of a name sign). However, this 2012 photo very likely depicts a PRE-restructuring host -- the program ran for decades at Ohio State University before splitting into the current two-site Otterbein/Rose-Hulman structure -- so it does NOT depict either current 2026 host and should only be used if S5A prioritizes self-identifying program imagery over current-campus accuracy. Rose-Hulman also has clean Commons campus photos (Category:Rose-Hulman_Institute_of_Technology, e.g. 'Moench Hall Rear View 2022.jpg') as a further alternate representing the other concurrent site.
